narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: The sacred writer: narration and the words that introduce speech; grave and restrained.

isaac.name: Isaac
isaac.note: Abraham's son, a boy carrying the wood; trusting and puzzled.

angel.name: Angel of the Lord
angel.note: The angel of the Lord calling from heaven; urgent, then solemn, delivering the Lord's oath.

1.t: After these things, God tempted Abraham, and said to him:

2.t: Take thy only begotten son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and go into the land of vision; and there thou shalt offer him for an holocaust upon one of the mountains which I will shew thee.

3.t: So Abraham rising up in the night, saddled his ass, and took with him two young men, and Isaac his son: and when he had cut wood for the holocaust, he went his way to the place which God had commanded him.

4.t: And on the third day, lifting up his eyes, he saw the place afar off.

5.t: And he said to his young men:
Stay you here with the ass; I and the boy will go with speed as far as yonder, and after we have worshipped, will return to you.

6.t: And he took the wood for the holocaust, and laid it upon Isaac his son; and he himself carried in his hands fire and a sword. And as they two went on together,

7.t: fire and wood: where is the victim for the holocaust?

8.t: God will provide himself a victim for an holocaust, my son.

9.t: And they came to the place which God had shewn him, where he built an altar, and laid the wood in order upon it; and when he had bound Isaac his son, he laid him on the altar upon the pile of wood.

10.t: And he put forth his hand, and took the sword, to sacrifice his son.

11.t: And behold, an angel of the Lord from heaven called to him, saying:

12.t: Lay not thy hand upon the boy, neither do thou any thing to him: now I know that thou fearest God, and hast not spared thy only begotten son for my sake.
12.q: the angel speaks in God's person ("for my sake"); kept with the angel

13.t: Abraham lifted up his eyes, and saw behind his back a ram, amongst the briers, sticking fast by the horns, which he took and offered for a holocaust instead of his son.

14.t: And he called the name of that place, The Lord seeth. Whereupon, even to this day, it is said: In the mountain the Lord will see.

15.t: And the angel of the Lord called to Abraham a second time from heaven, saying:

16.t: By my own self have I sworn, saith the Lord: because thou hast done this thing, and hast not spared thy only begotten son for my sake:
16.q: the Lord's oath delivered by the angel ("saith the Lord" is part of what the angel says); kept with the angel

17.t: I will bless thee, and I will multiply thy seed as the stars of heaven, and as the sand that is by the sea shore; thy seed shall possess the gates of their enemies.

18.t: And in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed, because thou hast obeyed my voice.

19.t: Abraham returned to his young men, and they went to Bersabee together, and he dwelt there.

20.t: After these things, it was told Abraham, that Melcha also had borne children to Nachor his brother.

21.t: Hus, the firstborn, and Buz, his brother, and Camuel the father of the Syrians,

22.t: And Cased, and Azau, and Pheldas, and Jedlaph,

23.t: And Bathuel, of whom was born Rebecca: these eight did Melcha bear to Nachor, Abraham's brother.

24.t: And his concubine, named Roma, bore Tabee, and Gaham, and Tahas, and Maacha.
